extracted.intended_audience: Florida state agency officials, regulators, attorneys, and stakeholders involved in rulemaking and administrative hearings
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes statutory requirements, deadlines, exceptions, and procedural rules in Florida's Administrative Procedure Act (Chapter 120) relevant to agency rulemaking, regulatory plans, notices, hearings, and special-area exceptions. Useful for agencies preparing rules, lawyers litigating administrative actions, and stakeholders tracking notice-and-comment obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory plan content and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must prepare and publish a regulatory plan identifying laws for which rulemaking is necessary and related information; certifications relating to review of a board's regulatory plan may cover multiple boards or commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must identify laws in the regulatory plan pursuant to subparagraph (1)(a)1.; a certification may relate to more than one board or commission; Department of Health must file certifications for boards under s.20.43(3)(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for notice of rule development (annual)
rubrics_metrics.description: By November 1 of each year, an agency must publish a notice of rule development for each law identified in the agency’s regulatory plan for which rulemaking is necessary but no notice of rule development has yet been published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites s.120.54(2); applies to laws reported in the regulatory plan pursuant to subparagraph (1)(a)1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to publish proposed rule (April 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each law identified in the regulatory plan as requiring implementing rulemaking, the agency must publish a notice of proposed rule by April 1 of the year following the regulatory plan deadline, subject to specified extension procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may extend this deadline by publishing a notice of extension in the Florida Administrative Register that cites the applicable notice of rule development and includes a concise statement identifying issues causing the delay; extension expires on October 1 after the April 1 deadline unless further extended by the next regulatory plan identification or concluded by the plan; regulatory plans may be corrected at any time and corrections must be noticed in the Florida Administrative Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of compliance and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall file a certification with the legislative committee upon compliance with the notice-of-rule-development deadline and upon filing a notice of deadline extension or regulatory plan correction; a certification may relate to more than one notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifications must note the date(s) of compliance and may relate to multiple notices or contemporaneous acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementing the regulatory plan after new law
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication of the regulatory plan, an agency must supplement the plan within 30 days after a bill becomes law if the law (enacted before the next regular session) substantively modifies the agency’s specifically delegated legal duties, unless the law affects most agencies as identified by the Governor or Attorney General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplement must include the information required in paragraph (1)(a) and be published as required in subsection (2); no certification or delivery to the committee is required, but the agency must publish notice of the supplement in the Florida Administrative Register and provide a hyperlink on its website; for laws reported in a supplement, if rulemaking is necessary the agency must publish a notice of rule development by the later of the Nov 1 deadline or 60 days after enactment, and a proposed rule by the later of the Apr 1 deadline or 120 days after enactment; proposed-rule deadlines may be extended to the following Oct 1 per subsection (5); if proposed rule not filed by Oct 1, law included in a supplement must be included in next annual plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure-to-comply explanation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency fails to comply with certain regulatory-plan notice filing or proposed-rule publication requirements, it must, within 15 days after written demand from the committee or a legislative committee chair, deliver a written explanation of reasons for noncompliance to the committee, President of the Senate, Speaker of the House, and requesting committee chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to failure to comply with paragraph (2)(a) or subsection (5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Administrative Hearings — impartial assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: A hearing in which the Division of Administrative Hearings is a party may not be conducted by an administrative law judge assigned by the division; an attorney assigned by the Administration Commission shall be the hearing officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding s.120.57(1)(a). This is intended to avoid a division-assigned ALJ presiding over matters where the division itself is a party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Financial Regulation application and hearing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings for issuance/denial/renewal/amendment of licenses or approvals under Title XXXVIII, the Office of Financial Regulation must publish notice of application in the Florida Administrative Register within 21 days of receipt; interested persons have 21 days after publication to request a hearing; failure to request within 21 days waives the right to a hearing (subject to certain exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a hearing is requested, the applicant or licensee must publish, at its own cost, a notice of the hearing in a newspaper of general circulation in the affected area (format/size may be specified by rule); applications for certain financial institution licenses must be approved or denied within 180 days after receipt (or be deemed approved subject to statutory conditions), with a one-year rule for applications involving foreign nationals owning/control ≥10% of voting securities or acquiring control; when agency refers an application to the Division for hearing, the ALJ must submit a written report of findings and evidentiary rulings and each party gets at least 10 days to file written exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Revenue — assessments and taxpayer-contest procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: An assessment of tax, penalty, or interest by the Department of Revenue is not a final order under the chapter; in administrative proceedings to contest assessments the taxpayer is the 'petitioner' and the Department the 'respondent' (with specified exceptions); the department's burden is limited to showing that an assessment was made and the factual/legal grounds for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to filing a petition, the taxpayer must pay amounts not being contested; failure to pay uncontested amount results in dismissal and a 25% additional penalty; jurisdictional requirements of s.72.011(2) and (3)(a) apply; collection/enforcement of contested amount is stayed upon filing a petition; prevailing party may recover legal costs including reasonable attorney’s fees if the losing party fails to raise a justiciable issue of law or fact; on judicial review, court may award attorney’s fees if Dept improperly rejected or modified a conclusion of law; proceedings to establish paternity/child support have special venue and review rules and final orders entered by the Division’s ALJ may be enforced under s.120.69 or other prescribed methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational units — exclusions and alternative notice methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Many provisions of the chapter do not apply to educational units: district school boards may adopt rules to implement general powers; preparation or modification of curricula and certain statewide tests/test scoring/testing procedures are not rules; educational units need not include full text of rules in notices or publish notices in the Florida Administrative Register but must notify affected persons by specified alternative means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative notice must be by publication in a newspaper of general circulation in affected area, by mail to persons/organizations who requested advance notice, and by posting in appropriate places so intended classes of persons are duly notified; educational units (other than the Florida School for the Deaf and the Blind) are not required to make filings with the committee for documents required by s.120.54 or s.120.55(1)(a)4.; educational-unit hearings involving student disciplinary suspensions/expulsions may be conducted by the units; certain notice requirements (e.g., 14-day notice) may be waived in student disciplinary hearings by the agency head or hearing officer; students are not persons subject to regulation for purposes of petitioning for variance/waiver under s.120.542; special meeting agendas for district school boards must be prepared upon calling but not less than 48 hours prior to meeting for certain meetings under s.1001.372(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prisoners and parolees — limits on participation and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Prisoners (per s.944.02) are not considered parties in proceedings except certain enumerated types and may not seek judicial review under s.120.68 of other agency action; parolees similarly are not parties regarding rescission or revocation of parole; prisoners may be limited to written statements in some rulemaking contexts and preliminary hearings for parole revocation must have no less than 7 days' notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prisoners are not eligible to seek an administrative determination of an agency statement under s.120.56(4); subsection (3)(b) allows the Department of Corrections to limit prisoner participation to written submissions concerning intended action on any department rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation of professions — sexual misconduct evidence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings against licensed professionals or licensure applicants involving allegations of sexual misconduct: victim testimony need not be corroborated; specific instances of prior consensual sexual activity by the victim with persons other than the offender are inadmissible unless narrowly shown in camera to be mistaken identity or highly similar pattern relevant to consent; reputation evidence relating to a victim’s prior sexual conduct is inadmissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding s.120.569(2)(g); the rules set evidentiary protections for victims and limit admissibility of prior sexual conduct evidence with specified exceptions determined by in-camera findings to the administrative law judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hunting and fishing — agency action not a rule with adequate notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency action that alters established hunting/fishing seasons or alters established annual saltwater harvest limits (when alteration procedure is set out by Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission rule) is not a 'rule' under the chapter provided the action is adequately noticed in the affected area via newspaper publication or electronic media broadcasting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a limited pathway for agencies to alter seasons/harvest limits outside formal rulemaking if adequate local notice is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk impact statement requirement for health-related rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Environmental Protection must prepare a risk impact statement for any rule proposed for approval by the Environmental Regulation Commission that establishes or changes standards or criteria based on impacts/effects upon human health; the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services must do likewise for any proposed rule establishing standards or criteria based on human health impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions: does not apply to rules adopted pursuant to federally delegated/mandated programs where rules are identical/substantially identical to federal regulations; does not apply to emergency rules; agencies must prepare and publish notice of availability of a clear and concise risk impact statement that explains the public health risk addressed and identifies/summarizes the source(s) of scientific information used in the evaluation; subsection does not create a new cause of action or diminish existing bases for challenging a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Florida Building Commission — no waivers; alternative means criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Florida Building Commission may not accept petitions for waiver or variance and may not grant any waiver or variance from Florida Building Code requirements; the Commission must adopt criteria and procedures in the Code for alternative means of compliance and appeals from denials of alternative means go to local boards and may be appealed to the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding s.120.542; Commission and hearing officer panels may conduct proceedings to review decisions of local building code officials in accordance with s.553.775(3)(c); s.120.541(3) does not apply to adoption of amendments and the triennial update to the Florida Building Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Fire Marshal and Dept. of Transportation limited-application exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 120.541(3) does not apply to adoption of amendments and the triennial update to the Florida Fire Prevention Code (State Fire Marshal); sections 120.54(3)(b) and 120.541 do not apply to adjustment of tolls under s.338.165(3) (Department of Transportation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are specific statutory carve-outs exempting certain code updates or toll adjustments from specified notice/adoption provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Florida Gaming Control Commission — limited hearing requirements for certain infractions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gaming Control Commission is exempt from ss.120.569 and 120.57(1)(a) hearing and notice requirements, but only for stewards/judges/boards of judges when hearings are to impose fines or suspensions (not revocations) and only for specified violations; the Commission must adopt rules establishing alternative procedures, including a hearing upon reasonable notice, for enumerated violations (drug use in animals/players, race-fixing, assault, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions apply only for listed paragraphs (a)-(f); the Commission must still adopt alternative procedures and provide reasonable notice for hearings on these violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Law Enforcement policies excluded from 'rule' definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Law enforcement policies and procedures relating to active criminal intelligence/investigative information management, undercover investigation management and identities, recruitment/management of confidential informants, surveillance techniques and personnel selection, hostage safety/release, security for public figures, and witness protection are not 'rules' under the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding s.120.57(1)(a); this preserves confidentiality and operational flexibility for law enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles — licensing and wrecker hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings regarding driver licensing under chapter 322 need not be conducted by an ALJ assigned by the Division; cancellation/suspension/revocation of a driver license may be effected by personal delivery or first-class mail per s.322.251; hearings to deny/suspend/remove wrecker operators from the wrecker rotation may be conducted by a hearing officer appointed by the Division director rather than an ALJ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding s.120.57(1)(a) and s.120.60(5); establishes alternative hearing officer arrangements and service methods specific to driver licensing and wrecker operator actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Children and Families — alternative hearing officer authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings conducted within the Department of Children and Families in execution of certain social and economic programs (formerly under Division of Family Services) need not be conducted by an ALJ assigned by the Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding s.120.57(1)(a); the department may use internal hearing officers for specified programmatic hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Health — limited use of ALJs for professional regulation matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal hearings related to regulation of professions (chapter 456) within the Department of Health or Agency for Health Care Administration may not be conducted by the State Surgeon General, the Secretary of Health Care Administration, or a board/member of a board; certain program hearings (e.g., WIC, Child Care Food Program) need not be by an ALJ and the Dept. of Health may contract with Department of Children and Families for a hearing officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding s.120.57(1)(a); distinguishes between who may preside and permits contracting for hearing officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Employees Relations Commission and certification exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings within the jurisdiction of the Public Employees Relations Commission need not be conducted by an ALJ assigned by the Division; s.120.60 does not apply to certification of employee organizations under s.447.307.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding s.120.57(1)(a); creates exceptions for collective bargaining/employee-organization certification processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Economic Opportunity — reemployment appeals exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulemaking provisions of the chapter do not apply to reemployment assistance appeals referees; uniform rules of procedure do not apply to appeal proceedings under chapter 443 by the Reemployment Assistance Appeals Commission, special deputies, or referees; hearings under chapter 443 may not be conducted by an ALJ assigned by the Division but instead by the Commission, referees, Department, or special deputies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding ss.120.54 and 120.57(1)(a) and 120.54(5); provides alternate adjudicative structures for unemployment/reemployment appeals.
